clue.text: Time limit that rules out all telephone conversation

definitions.meaning: the latest moment by which something must be done
a phone line that has gone dead carries no talk at all

explanation.surface: A cut-off point that bans any chatting on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a final cut-off for work, and literally a telephone connection that is dead, so nobody can talk.

clue.text: Spot a rising doctor, one who is getting on

parts.note: a spot is a dot

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: Notice a doctor going up in the world, someone advancing in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DR upwards to RD. 'getting on' is ageing, not succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is a feeble-minded old person, someone advanced in age.

clue.text: Acts in a peculiar way-obviously!

indicators.note: in a peculiar way says the letters are set out oddly, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Behaves strangely, as is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition (clownish capers are acts done oddly) and the wordplay, rearranging ACTS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are absurd or grotesque capers, behaviour that is plainly odd.

clue.text: Neither do they spin 51 fibs

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
fibs are lies

explanation.surface: Fifty-one untruths, none of them spun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the Sermon on the Mount: 'Consider the lilies of the field... they toil not, neither do they spin.'
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of Matthew, these flowers of the field are said not to toil or weave thread.

clue.text: Sentry with a luminous face for a time

definitions.meaning: a guard on duty after dark
a timepiece with a glowing dial, readable after dark

explanation.surface: A guard whose glowing face tells the time.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the guard duty kept after dark; the other is a timepiece with a glow-in-the-dark dial, read in bed.

clue.text: Pursued trade as a metal engraver

definitions.meaning: to chase metal is to ornament it by engraving or embossing, so this is the craftsman's past-tense verb

explanation.surface: Someone followed a career engraving metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunted down is one sense; the other is the metalworker's term for engraved or embossed ornament on silver and similar.

clue.text: If not a topper, then bowler is needed to perform it

definitions.text: If not a topper, then bowler is needed to perform it

parts.words: If not a topper, then bowler is needed to perform it
parts.note: a conjuror pulls a rabbit from a top hat; in cricket a bowler takes three wickets with successive balls

explanation.surface: A conjuror needing some sort of headgear for the act.
explanation.walkthrough: Topper and bowler both look like hats; the second is a cricketer, for whom three wickets with consecutive balls earns this feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's feat with a top hat, and in cricket three wickets taken by one bowler with successive deliveries.

clue.text: A boy smothered in dirt has dressing

indicators.note: smothered in means covered over by, so the dirt surrounds the boy

parts.note: dirt is soil
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy covered in mud is wearing bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smothered in' signals the container. 'dressing' suggests a bandage for a wound; it is the kind poured on salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This oil is used for dressing salads, a culinary dressing.

clue.text: Drops of French perfumery

parts.note: de is French for of
perfumery here is scents collectively

explanation.surface: Little drops of French perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' suggests drips of scent; it means falls or downward slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Descents are falls or downward slopes, drops in height.

clue.text: TT League organised period of tuition

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A table-tennis league laid on a spell of coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges TT plus LEAGUE. TT also suggests the Isle of Man motorcycle races, adding to the sporting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guardianship given by a tutor, a spell of teaching.

clue.text: They add to a clown's standing

definitions.text: They add to a clown's standing

parts.words: They add to a clown's standing
parts.note: standing here means literal height: circus clowns walk on tall wooden poles strapped to their legs, which raise them up

explanation.surface: Things that boost a clown's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall poles with footrests worn by circus performers make them stand much higher, adding to their standing height.

clue.text: Make a new effort to amuse oneself

definitions.text: Make a new effort to amuse oneself

parts.words: Make a new effort to amuse oneself
parts.note: read with a hyphen the word means build again; read as one word it means to take leisure and enjoy oneself

explanation.surface: Trying once more to have some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it is to create anew; unhyphenated it is to refresh oneself with amusement, recreation.

clue.text: Card game that ends with two banks

definitions.meaning: a trick-taking game for four players in two partnerships
a span over a river has a bank at each end

explanation.surface: A card game finishing with two bank accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the partnership card game and also the structure crossing water, which rests on a riverbank at either end.

clue.text: First-rate face-saver for anyone in charge

parts.note: super means excellent
a visor is a shield protecting the face

explanation.surface: Top-quality ways of saving face for whoever runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saver' usually means a way of avoiding embarrassment; here it is literal protective gear for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees others, the person with authority over a team.

clue.text: Post-graduate teachers take in extra share to provide written work

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a postgraduate degree

indicators.note: take in means the teachers' union holds the share inside itself

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
scrip is a certificate for extra shares issued free to shareholders, as in a scrip issue

explanation.surface: Graduate tutors grab a bonus allocation to produce a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' signals the container. NUT, the National Union of Teachers, was Britain's largest teaching union; a scrip issue gives shareholders extra shares free.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is an author's text, a written or typed work before printing.

clue.text: Chance police department being taken in by foreign coinage

indicators.note: being taken in by means held inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin used abroad, in the US and the eurozone
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Fortune has a detective squad duped by counterfeit currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken in by' puts CID inside A CENT. 'taken in' suggests being fooled, not contained.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something happening by luck, without design.

clue.text: Jeopardise make-up

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Jeopardise make-up (8)': 'Jeopardise' defines ENDANGER but 'make-up' supplies no letters, so the wordplay appears cut short in the OCR; a search of the exact text found nothing.

clue.text: Older but confused and worried

indicators.note: confused means jumbled up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ageing yet muddled and anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubled means anxious or distressed in mind.

clue.text: Shrunk from being bound to undertake the job

definitions.meaning: legally committed by agreement to carry out work

explanation.surface: Someone diminished by being obliged to take on a task.
explanation.definitionFit: It means drawn together and smaller, and also signed up by a formal agreement to do work.

clue.text: Albert raising cap to a woolly beast

parts.note: Al is a short form of Albert

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Albert doffs his cap to a woolly animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns CAP upwards into PAC; 'raising cap' looks like a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American relative of the llama, kept for its fleece.

clue.text: Language suggesting elegance

explanation.surface: A tongue that hints at refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalised it is the tongue of Poland; lowercase it means refinement or shine.

clue.text: Maybe a big boxer likely to erupt

definitions.text: Maybe a big boxer likely to erupt

parts.words: Maybe a big boxer likely to erupt
parts.note: boxer read as someone who packs things in crates, and also a volcano mouth that may blow

explanation.surface: A heavyweight fighter with a short temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' wants to be a fighter; it is one who packs goods into crates. A volcano's mouth is the part that erupts.
explanation.definitionFit: One who packs crates is literally a big boxer, and a volcano's bowl-shaped mouth is where eruption happens.

clue.text: One automobile America regarded as being a classic high-flier

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an automobile is a car
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A single American car seen as a vintage top performer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth he flew too close to the sun on wings of wax, so he is literally a high-flier from classical legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure from classical Greek myth flew so high on wax wings that they melted, a literal high flyer.

clue.text: One who lied over dissimulation maybe

definitions.text: One who lied over dissimulation maybe

indicators.note: dissimulation is disguise, so the letters are disguised by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who kept lying about faking things.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a wrongdoer, a liar being one example, while 'dissimulation maybe' disguises LIED OVER by rearranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual liar is a kind of wrongdoer, a person who commits wicked acts.

clue.text: Swallow returning north-east to Arab war zone

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation runs back the other way

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
the Gulf, the Persian Gulf region, scene of the Gulf Wars

explanation.surface: A bird flying back north-east to the battlefields of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the migrating bird; it is the verb meaning to devour.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to overwhelm and consume completely, as the sea might gulp down a boat.

clue.text: Yet world-weary people may regard such literature as captivating

definitions.text: Yet world-weary people may regard such literature as captivating

parts.words: Yet world-weary people may regard such literature as captivating
parts.note: fiction offering a flight from reality appeals to the weary, captivating them even though it lets them break free

explanation.surface: Tired souls find a particular sort of book enthralling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction that offers flight from everyday reality is the kind a person fed up with the world enjoys.

clue.text: A vehement speech for one in commerce

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the business word

parts.note: commerce is trade
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An angry rant on behalf of somebody working in business.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry harangue, a passionate denunciation.

clue.text: Nose rest

definitions.meaning: the nose is the organ one inhales through

explanation.definitionFit: The nose is something that draws in air, and a pause to recover one's wind is a short break.
